title: Skill-sprint Hiring + 21-day Onboard Catalyst (pilot)
content:
Purpose
This doc is an operational playbook for running a short, focused hiring + onboarding experiment we call a "skill-sprint". Goal: reduce time-to-impact for IC hires by structuring interview signals around the first 21 days of work and giving a tight, measurable onboarding plan.

Intended audience
- People Ops (owner)
- Hiring managers and interviewers
- Engineering managers who will run pilot pods
- Solutions / Platform teams (early adopters)

High-level hypothesis
If we align hiring signals directly with the first 21-day contribution loop (fast tasks, mentoring, code-read, shallow ship), we can:
- Improve new hire ramp velocity by 20–30%
- Reduce biased signal noise by assessing concrete, relevant skills
- Shorten time-to-offer by focusing interviews on job-shaped problems

When to use this playbook
- Backfill or new IC roles where early product impact matters (platform infra, SRE, serving-runtime squads)
- When hiring volume moderate (2–4 hires / quarter) and we can staff a consistent interview panel

Checklist: pre-hire (People Ops + hiring manager)
- [ ] Define the 21-day impact goal for the role (one clear deliverable)
- [ ] Create the job-shaped sample task (3–6 hours equivalent) and acceptance criteria
- [ ] Assemble interview panel (3 interviewers: core skill, systems thinking, culture/operations)
- [ ] Prepare rubric and shared scoring sheet (section below)
- [ ] Create first-21-days onboarding plan draft and mentor pairing (names + backup)
- [ ] Add linked artifacts to candidate packet (Confluence page + GH sandbox + ticket stub)

Interview format (pilot)
1) Recruiter screen (30m) — fit + logistics
2) Task take-home (4–6 hours) — job-shaped, optional pair session at candidate request
3) Panel loop (~3 interviews, 45m each) — focused prompts aligned to 21-day deliverable
4) Hiring manager deep-dive (30m) — role expectations, signal synthesis

Scoring rubric (single-sheet, 1-5) — flattened for easy aggregation
- Technical competence (practical): 1-5 — can they ship a small, safe change end-to-end?
- Systems thinking (design + tradeoffs): 1-5 — can they reason about latency, cost, failure modes?
- Operational ownership (oncall, runbooks): 1-5 — do they anticipate support needs?
- Collaboration & communication: 1-5 — can they drive async work and handoffs?
- Learning velocity & curiosity: 1-5 — will they close knowledge gaps in the first 21 days?
- Cultural fit / values alignment: 1-5

Accept / hold / decline thresholds (pilot)
- Fast accept: avg >= 4.0 and no score <= 2
- Consider with manager: avg 3.5-3.99 or one 2 flagged but strong compensating signals
- Decline: avg < 3.5 or any severe operational risk (e.g., cannot own incidents)

Interview question bank (examples tuned to Redwood inference use-cases)
- Job-shaped take-home: Add a prefix-KV cache invalidation for a toy inference route. Provide a small repo that simulates requests; acceptance: tests + short design note. (Signal: code hygiene, testing, latency-awareness)
- Design prompt (systems): You have a model variant rollout and capacity limit. Sketch routing strategy to meet latency SLOs while minimizing cost. (Signal: routing + SLA tradeoffs)
- Operational scenario (onsite): A spike causes repeated OOMs on dedicated GPUs. How do you triage and mitigate? (Signal: incident response, metrics chosen)
- Collaboration prompt: Describe a time you onboarded a cross-functional partner and what the kickoff artifacts looked like. (Signal: async comms, ownership)

Interviewers: calibration notes
- Use concrete examples from the take-home when available. Score behaviors not personalities.
- If unsure, call a 10m post-interview sync with another panelist (capture dissenting signals).
- Avoid vague adjectives: instead of "strong communicator" list the evidence (e.g., produced runbook, led handoff)

Offer + pre-accept plan
- Before offer: hiring manager to outline first 21-day deliverable and high-level success metrics in the offer packet (this reduces mismatch)
- Include a tentative mentor calendar and immediate access list (GH sandbox + dev cluster + Slack channels)

Onboarding: 21-day micro-sprint (overview)
Principle: make the first weeks a loop of small, shipped outcomes + deliberate learning. Each week ends with a visible deliverable.
Week 0 (day 0–3): access + context + micro-commit
- Day 0: welcome + hardware/access checklist (KMS, infra VPN, repo perms, SSO)
- Day 1: role kickoff w/ manager (30m) — define 21-day deliverable; mentor introduced
- Day 2: dev environment + run the toy integration test; small doc patch as micro-commit
- Day 3: pair with mentor to land first small change into a sandbox PR
Week 1 (day 4–10): measurement + small ship
- Complete the job-shaped task in production-like sandbox; write a 1-page design note
- Deliverable: merged sandbox PR + CI green + short demo to pod (15m)
Week 2 (day 11–17): integrate + observe
- Owner a small route change: metrics dashboard + alerting baseline set up
- Run a short load test and capture latency/cost delta; propose a mitigation if regression > 5%
Week 3 (day 18–21): handoff + future plan
- Final deliverable: small shipped change to staging or gated prod + 1-page runbook + async retro
- Manager + mentor evaluation: go/no-go on autonomy signals (see evaluation checklist)

Onboard evaluation checklist (end of day 21) — manager fills in
- Shipped deliverable: yes/no + link
- Tests & CI health: passing / flaky / failing
- Docs & runbook: complete / partial / none
- Mentor readiness: confident / needs more mentoring
- Needs: list of 3 things to unblock in next 30d
- Recommendation: green / amber (needs upskill) / red (remediation)

Mentor playbook (concise)
- 1hr/day first 5 days pairing; then 3×/week drop-in
- Do a walkthrough of the code path, infra, and common latencies to watch for
- Introduce the new hire to the oncall rotation and incident postmortem staples
- Commit to a 21-day check-in doc with clear next actions

Signals we track (pilot metrics)
- Time-to-first-merged-PR (target <= 7 days)
- Number of production-like deploys in first 21 days (target >=1 gated)
- Ramp NPS (new-hire survey day 7, day 21)
- Hiring funnel: time-to-offer, candidate drop rate after take-home

Known risks / tradeoffs
- Extra interviewer prep overhead — mitigate by standardizing rubrics and reusing tasks
- Hiring bias risk: take-homes can advantage candidates with free time; offer pair-alternatives
- Manager bandwidth: 21-day deliverable requires manager + mentor alignment up-front

TODOs (next steps for pilot)
- [ ] Lock 2 pilot roles (infra + console) by Jan 15
- [ ] Create standardized GH sandbox + infra-stub by Jan 31 (owner: Diego)
- [ ] Run interviewer calibration session (1hr) and save recording to Confluence
- [ ] Draft candidate-facing FAQ about take-home expectations (owner: People Ops)

Notes to self (author)
- Keep the playbook intentionally lightweight — avoid a huge checklist that slows managers.
- Want a small dashboard for pilot metrics; can reuse hiring dashboard widgets in Console team.
- Capture one anonymized case study after pilot to build a more repeatable kit.

Appendix: sample micro-commit checklist (to give to candidate & new hire)
- Repo cloned and test suite runs locally
- Small PR (<= 20 lines) that includes a test and description
- Add one line in Confluence: "what I learned and what surprised me"

End of doc.

Feedback welcome — ping in #people-ops or directly to me (aisha@redwood.example)
